paper_id: Towards Effective Next POI Prediction_ Spatial and Semantic Augmentation with Remote Sensing Data
title: Towards Effective Next POI Prediction: Spatial and Semantic Augmentation with Remote Sensing Data
motivation: Existing POI prediction models neglect environmental influences (road density, land usage) that shape human mobility patterns.
problem_framing: Define three challenges: (1) neglecting environmental factors, (2) ineffective spatial graph due to uneven POI distribution, (3) failing to separate spatial and semantic intents in a unified prediction framework.
key_insight: Remote sensing imagery acts as a warehouse of environmental context (land use, urban morphology) that enriches tile representations beyond POI density alone; quad-tree with road network edges solves both granularity and connectivity problems.
method_signature: TSPN-RA: two-step prediction (tile selection → POI ranking) with quad-tree road-graph (QR-P) and CNN-encoded remote sensing tile embeddings.
evaluation_criteria: Recall@K and MRR on four real-world LBSN datasets (Gowalla, Foursquare, NYC, TKY); inference efficiency (FLOPs, memory, training time).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Introducing 20% noise into satellite imagery causes the majority of tiles to appear in inland areas, leading to failed predictions — imagery quality directly impacts spatial filtering.
